related_questions.question: How can I check someone's immigration status?

text_blocks.snippet: To check someone's immigration status in the U.S., you can use the USCIS Case Status Online tool or the ICE Detainee Locator for individuals in detention. If you need to request immigration records, you can explore options through the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) or Privacy Act.
Using the USCIS Case Status Online Tool:

list.snippet: Navigate to the USCIS website: Go to the USCIS Case Status Online page.
Enter the receipt number: Locate the 13-character receipt number (three letters followed by 10 numbers) on the application or petition notice from USCIS and enter it, omitting any dashes.
Check the status: Click "Check Status" to view the current status of the case.
Go to the ICE website: Access the Online Detainee Locator System (ODLS) on the ICE website.
Enter details: Provide the individual's name, country of birth, and birth date, or their 9-digit A-number.
Search: The system will display information about the individual's location in ICE custody.

list.title: 1. Submit a request:
list.snippet: Use the USCIS online FOIA system to request your own immigration records, another person's records with their permission, or agency policies and communications.

list.title: 2. Provide information:
list.snippet: Include necessary details like the individual's name, date of birth, and any relevant case or file numbers.

list.title: MyUSCIS Account:
list.snippet: You can create a MyUSCIS account to manage and track your immigration cases, according to USCIS.

list.title: SAVE Program:
list.snippet: Registered government agencies can use the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program to verify immigration status when applicants seek benefits or licenses.

list.title: State or Local Agencies:
list.snippet: Some state or local agencies may have their own systems for verifying immigration status, so check their websites for information if you are seeking a benefit or license from one of these agencies.
